newsitem.title: CHINA: U.S. says extends China textile deadline by a day.
newsitem.headline: U.S. says extends China textile deadline by a day.

text.p: The United States has extended by one day a deadline for agreement on a new textile accord with China, chief U.S. negotiator Rita Hayes said on Saturday.

"I felt like it was important to extend it, the deadline, for one day... so we could get a fresh start this morning," Hayes said as she left for last-ditch talks with Chinese officials on renewal of a 1994 textile accord and a dispute over U.S. penalties on Chinese exports.
"We did not complete the agreement...so we felt like we'd have one extra day to complete it," she said.
The Sino-U.S. textile pact had been scheduled to expire on December 31 but was extended one month to give both sides time to hammer out a compromise.
Before Hayes's statement, the previous deadline after which tit-for-tat trade penalties were to have taken effect was midnight January 31 Eastern Standard Time (0500 GMT Saturday).
